full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that the suit land originally belonged to Nabid Ali whose name was recorded in R.S. khatian. That one Abdul Latif was the superior landlord of the suit land who used to receive rent from Nabid Ali since 1925. After acquisition of rent receiving interest by the government Nabid Ali continued payment of rent in favour of the government for the suit land. Nabid Ali died leaving behind wife Sharfun Nessa, two sons Saleh Ahmed and Siddique Ahmed and one daughter Salema Khatun. P.S. khatian No. 3345 was prepared in the name of the said heirs of Nabid Ali. On 10.07.1976 the said heirs of Nabid Ali sold the suit land to the plaintiff by two registered kabala and delivered possession of the suit land also in favour of the plaintiff. That the defendant No. 1, Chittagong Zilla Parishad has no right, title and possession in the suit land. Inspite of that the defendant Nio.1, claiming title in the suit land, is trying to issue licence in respect of the suit land in favour of the defendant No. 2 and thus the plaintiff was compelled to file the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement. The material case of these defendants was that the suit land belonged to the defendant No. 1. That C.S. khatian No. 3100 was duly recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 and Mr. Abdul Latif took temporary lease of the suit land from the defendant No. 1 and the R.S. khatian No. 3121 was prepared in the name of Abdul Latif. That Abdul Latif used to possess the suit land through bargadar Nabid Ali. That Nabid Ali, with ill motive to grab the suit land, recorded the same in his name in R.S. khatian and also in subsequent P.S. and B.S. khatians in collusion with survey staff. That Nabid Ali being a mere bargadar had no title in the suit land and as such the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title and possession in the suit land by virtue of his so called purchase from the heirs of Nabid Ali. 

 9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel for the petitioner has mainly argued to the effect that the lower appellate court and the High Court Division have committed great error in not considering at all the fact that Abdul Latif was a ejaradar for a limited period under the Chittagong Zilla Parishad, that though the relevant khatian-the exhibit-1 and the exhibit-A clearly showed that Nabid Ali was a mere "dakhalkar" under Abdul Latif and Abdul Latif was a ejaradar under Chittagong Zilla Parishad for a period of 5 years only but both the High Court Division and the lower appellate court have failed to take into consideration these documentary evidence at all and also to comprehend the same and thus have failed to come to a right decision. Drawing our attention to exhibit-A the learned Counsel for the petitioner has argued that this exhibit-A proves clearly that Chittagong District Board was the owner of the suit land and under this landlord Abdul Latif was a mere ejaradar for a period of five years only from 1926-1931 and in the circumstances Abdul Latif had no right to settle the suit land to Nabid Ali. The learned Counsel has contended that this exhibit-A along with exhibit-1 proves also the case of the contesting defendants that Nabid Ali was a mere "dakhalkar" under Abdul Latif. The learned Counsel has contended also that long before promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the ejara right of Abdul Latif ceased to exist and as such the Chittagong Zilla Parishad took back the khas possession of the suit land and the suit land remained in the khas possession of the defendant No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 subsequently leased out the suit land to defendant No. 2 lawfully. The learned Counsel has argued to the effect also that there are sufficient evidence on record-both oral and documentary which proved that Chittagong Zilla Parishad was in possession of the suit land along with other lands and has been possessing those lands by giving temporary lease to different persons; but the lower appellate court and also the High Court Division have failed to appreciate these evidence on record and consequently arrived at a wrong decision which cannot be sustained in law. 

 "I. Because the District Board being the tenant under Emperor of India and their tenancy being rent free and Abdul Latif being a ejaradar under the District Board for a limited period and Nabid Ali being a dakhalkar under said Abdul Latif and there being no materials to show that either Abdul Latif or Nabid Ali was in possession of the suit land at the time of acquisition of rent receiving interest under SAT Act, thus the plaintiff has not acquired any interest in the suit land by way of purchase from the heirs of Nabid Ali in the year 1976 and without considering the said aspect appellate court decreed the suit and the High Court Division erred in affirming the judgment of the appellate court. 

 II. Because in deciding the instant suit the court of appeal below has not taken into consideration that under section 2A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the interest of the local authority has been kept outside of acquisition under the said Act (39 DLR (AD) page-16).
